name: ratelimit
description: Rate limiting for HTTP services: token bucket, GCRA, fixed and sliding windows, a lock-free in-memory table, a SQLite store, RateLimit headers and a handler wrapper

api.name: TokenBucket
api.sig: pub type TokenBucket = {rate: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000000000, period_ms: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000000000000, burst: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000000000} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A token bucket that holds at most `burst` tokens and refills continuously at `rate` tokens per
`period_ms` (as golang.org/x/time/rate with a limit of rate / period and a burst). A request of
cost n takes n tokens. Build it with `token_bucket`, which checks that the arithmetic is exact.

api.name: Gcra
api.sig: pub type Gcra = {limit: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000000000, period_ms: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000000000000, burst: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000000000} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
The generic cell rate algorithm (as redis-cell): `limit` requests per `period_ms`, at most
`burst` of them at once. Its state is one number, the theoretical arrival time, kept in
microseconds. It allows the same requests as a token bucket with the same numbers. Build it
with `gcra`.

api.name: Window
api.sig: pub type Window = {limit: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000000000, window_ms: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000000000000} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A window of `window_ms` milliseconds in which at most `limit` cost units are allowed, for the
fixed and sliding window algorithms.

api.name: Policy
api.sig: pub type Policy = BucketPolicy{bucket: TokenBucket} | GcraPolicy{gcra: Gcra} | FixedWindow{window: Window} | SlidingLog{window: Window} | SlidingCounter{window: Window} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
The algorithm a limiter runs. `FixedWindow` counts per calendar window (cheap, but allows up to
twice the limit across a boundary), `SlidingLog` keeps every request in the window (exact, memory
grows with the limit), `SlidingCounter` weighs the previous window's count by how much of it
still overlaps (Cloudflare's approximation, two numbers of state; it assumes the previous
window's requests were spread evenly, rounds the weighted count up, and can allow more than the
limit in a sliding window only when they clustered at its end).

api.name: Hit
api.sig: pub type Hit = {at_ms: Int, cost: Int} derive Eq, Show, Json
api.doc: One allowed request in a sliding log.

api.name: State
api.sig: pub type State = BucketState{level: Int, at_ms: Int} | GcraState{tat_us: Int} | WindowState{start_ms: Int, count: Int} | LogState{hits: List[Hit]} | CounterState{start_ms: Int, prev: Int, curr: Int} derive Eq, Show, Json
api.doc:
The state a policy keeps per key. `fresh` makes the initial one; a state of another policy's
shape counts as fresh, so changing a key's policy starts it over.

api.name: Decision
api.sig: pub type Decision = {allowed: Bool, limit: Int, remaining: Int, reset_ms: Int, retry_after_ms: Int} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
The answer for one request. `limit` is the quota (the burst of a bucket), `remaining` what is
left of it after this request, `reset_ms` the time until the quota is whole again,
`retry_after_ms` 0 when allowed, the wait before a request of the same cost can succeed when
denied, or -1 when the cost is larger than the quota and can never succeed.

api.name: token_bucket
api.sig: fn token_bucket(rate: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000000000, period_ms: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000000000000, burst: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000000000) -> TokenBucket
api.doc: A token bucket after the x/time/rate convention: `rate` tokens per `period_ms`, `burst` at most.

api.name: gcra
api.sig: fn gcra(limit: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000000000, period_ms: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000000000000, burst: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000000000) -> Gcra
api.doc:
A GCRA policy: `limit` requests per `period_ms`, `burst` at once. The emission interval must be
at least a microsecond and the burst tolerance must fit in 2^62 microseconds.

api.name: window
api.sig: fn window(limit: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000000000, window_ms: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000000000000) -> Window
api.doc: `limit` per `window_ms`, for the window policies.

api.name: per_second
api.sig: fn per_second(n: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000000000) -> Policy
api.doc: `n` requests per second, with a burst of `n`, as a token bucket.

api.name: per_minute
api.sig: fn per_minute(n: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000000000) -> Policy
api.doc: `n` requests per minute, with a burst of `n`, as a token bucket.

api.name: per_hour
api.sig: fn per_hour(n: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 1000000000) -> Policy
api.doc: `n` requests per hour, with a burst of `n`, as a token bucket.

api.name: quota
api.sig: fn quota(p: Policy) -> Int
api.doc: The quota of a policy: the burst of a bucket or GCRA, the limit of a window.

api.name: window_ms
api.sig: fn window_ms(p: Policy) -> Int
api.doc:
The time in milliseconds over which the whole quota is granted: the window, or the time a
bucket takes to refill from empty (rounded up).

api.name: fresh
api.sig: fn fresh(p: Policy, now_ms: Int) -> State
api.doc: The state of a key that has not been seen, at `now_ms`.

api.name: decide
api.sig: fn decide(p: Policy, s: Opt[State], now_ms: Int, cost: Int where _ >= 0) -> (Decision, State)
api.doc:
Decides a request of `cost` units for a key in state `s` (none for a new key) at `now_ms`, and
returns the decision and the key's next state. A cost of 0 only reports the current status. A
clock that goes backwards never grants more: the state's own time is used instead.

api.name: simulate
api.sig: fn simulate(p: Policy, requests: List[(Int, Int)]) -> List[Decision]
api.doc:
Decides a whole sequence of requests `(now_ms, cost)` for one key from a fresh state; handy in
tests and simulations.

api.name: expires_at
api.sig: fn expires_at(p: Policy, s: State) -> Int
api.doc:
The absolute time in milliseconds after which `s` is the same as a fresh state, so a store may
forget the key.

api.name: Reservation
api.sig: pub type Reservation = {ok: Bool, cost: Int, delay_ms: Int, act_at_ms: Int} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A reservation of `cost` tokens: `ok` when it was granted, and then the request may act
`delay_ms` later, at `act_at_ms`.

api.name: tokens
api.sig: fn tokens(b: TokenBucket, s: Opt[State], now_ms: Int) -> Int
api.doc: The tokens in the bucket at `now_ms` (negative while reservations owe tokens), rounded down.

api.name: wait_ms
api.sig: fn wait_ms(b: TokenBucket, s: Opt[State], now_ms: Int, cost: Int where _ >= 0) -> Int
api.doc:
The wait in milliseconds until `cost` tokens are there, without taking them: 0 now, -1 if
`cost` is more than the burst.

api.name: reserve
api.sig: fn reserve(b: TokenBucket, s: Opt[State], now_ms: Int, cost: Int where _ >= 0, max_wait_ms: Int where _ >= 0) -> (Reservation, State)
api.doc:
Reserves `cost` tokens, letting the bucket go into debt, when they will be there within
`max_wait_ms`; the caller waits `delay_ms` and then acts. Otherwise nothing is reserved. As
x/time/rate's ReserveN with a deadline.

api.name: cancel
api.sig: fn cancel(b: TokenBucket, s: State, r: Reservation, now_ms: Int) -> State
api.doc:
Gives back the tokens of a granted reservation that has not acted yet (its time is after
`now_ms`), up to a full bucket. Unlike x/time/rate it does not subtract tokens later
reservations took, so a cancel may restore slightly more than a perfect ledger would.

api.name: Table
api.sig: pub type Table = new Slots
api.doc:
A fixed-size, lock-free table for the policies `memory_supported` accepts, shared by the
handlers of one process (they may share only atomics). Each slot is a pair of Atomic[Int]: the
key's 64-bit fingerprint and its packed state, updated with compare-and-swap, so a decision is
exact under any contention. A key is looked up in `probes` consecutive slots from the one its
hash names, claiming an empty one or one whose state has fully recovered (an idle key, whose
state equals a fresh one). When every probed slot is busy with other keys, the key shares its
home slot with them: sharing only ever denies earlier, never allows more. Size it at about
twice the number of keys active within one window; `used` shows the occupancy. It is opaque and
has no Eq or Show, because it holds atomics.

api.name: table
api.sig: fn table(slots: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 16777216, probes: Int where _ >= 1 and _ <= 64) -> Table ! conc
api.doc: A table of `slots` slots probing `probes` of them per key.

api.name: memory_supported
api.sig: fn memory_supported(p: Policy) -> Bool
api.doc:
Whether the in-memory table can run `p`: token buckets and GCRA (as GCRA) and fixed windows,
whose state fits in one 64-bit word. Sliding windows need the SQLite store.

api.name: as_gcra
api.sig: fn as_gcra(b: TokenBucket) -> Gcra
api.doc: The GCRA with the same numbers as a token bucket; both allow the same requests.

api.name: take
api.sig: fn take(t: Table, p: Policy, key: Str, now_ms: Int, cost: Int where _ >= 0) -> Decision ! conc, div
api.doc:
Decides a request of `cost` for `key` in the table at `now_ms`. Exact under concurrent calls:
the update is a compare-and-swap loop on the key's slot.

api.name: peek
api.sig: fn peek(t: Table, p: Policy, key: Str, now_ms: Int) -> Decision ! conc
api.doc: The status of `key` without taking anything (a cost of 0).

api.name: reset
api.sig: fn reset(t: Table, key: Str) -> Bool ! conc
api.doc: Forgets `key`'s state, as if it had never been seen: whether it was in the table.

api.name: used
api.sig: fn used(t: Table) -> Int ! conc
api.doc: How many slots hold a key.

api.name: SqlStore
api.sig: pub type SqlStore = {db: Db, table: Str} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
A SQLite table of states, one row per key with its JSON state and the time it expires. Every
decision is a transaction (BEGIN IMMEDIATE), so processes sharing the database file, and the
handlers of one process sharing the Db, never lose an update. Works with every policy.

api.name: valid_table_name
api.sig: fn valid_table_name(s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc:
Whether `s` can name the store's table: a letter or underscore, then letters, digits and
underscores, at most 63 characters.

api.name: sql_store
api.sig: fn sql_store(c: Db, table: Str where valid_table_name(_)) -> SqlStore ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: Opens the store in `c`, creating the table `table` (and its expiry index) when missing.

api.name: sql_take
api.sig: fn sql_take(s: SqlStore, p: Policy, key: Str, now_ms: Int, cost: Int where _ >= 0) -> Decision ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc:
Decides a request of `cost` for `key` at `now_ms` in one transaction, and stores the new state
when the request is allowed.

api.name: sql_peek
api.sig: fn sql_peek(s: SqlStore, p: Policy, key: Str, now_ms: Int) -> Decision ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: The status of `key` without taking anything; reads only.

api.name: sql_reset
api.sig: fn sql_reset(s: SqlStore, key: Str) -> Bool ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: Forgets `key`: whether it had a row.

api.name: sql_purge
api.sig: fn sql_purge(s: SqlStore, now_ms: Int) -> Int ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc:
Deletes the rows of keys whose state has fully recovered by `now_ms`; the number deleted.
Run it now and then (each decision only touches its own key).

api.name: sql_count
api.sig: fn sql_count(s: SqlStore) -> Int ! db, fail[DbErr]
api.doc: How many keys have a row.

api.name: Ip
api.sig: pub type Ip = V4{n: Int} | V6{hi: Int, lo: Int} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: An IP address: IPv4 as a 32-bit number, IPv6 as two 64-bit halves.

api.name: Cidr
api.sig: pub type Cidr = {ip: Ip, bits: Int} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: A network: an address and a prefix length.

api.name: parse_ip
api.sig: fn parse_ip(s: Str) -> Opt[Ip]
api.doc:
Parses an IPv4 address in dotted decimal (no leading zeros, which some parsers read as octal) or
an IPv6 address in any RFC 4291 text form, including `::` and a dotted IPv4 tail. Zone ids and
brackets are not accepted.

api.name: normalize
api.sig: fn normalize(ip: Ip) -> Ip
api.doc: An IPv4-mapped IPv6 address (`::ffff:192.0.2.1`) as the IPv4 address it maps; others unchanged.

api.name: ip_str
api.sig: fn ip_str(ip: Ip) -> Str
api.doc:
The text of an address: dotted decimal, or the RFC 5952 form of IPv6 (lower case, no leading
zeros, the longest run of zero groups as `::`).

api.name: parse_cidr
api.sig: fn parse_cidr(s: Str) -> Opt[Cidr]
api.doc:
Parses `addr/bits`, or a bare address as a single-address network. Host bits may be set; they
are ignored when matching.

api.name: cidr_contains
api.sig: fn cidr_contains(c: Cidr, ip: Ip) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `ip` is in the network `c`. IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses match IPv4 networks.

api.name: parse_cidrs
api.sig: fn parse_cidrs(xs: List[Str]) -> Opt[List[Cidr]]
api.doc: Parses a list of networks, skipping none: none if any entry is not a network.

api.name: private_networks
api.sig: fn private_networks() -> List[Cidr]
api.doc:
Loopback, private (RFC 1918, RFC 4193), link-local and carrier-grade NAT networks: the usual
addresses of proxies inside a deployment, to pass as `trusted`.

api.name: ip_from_xff
api.sig: fn ip_from_xff(req: Request, trusted: List[Cidr]) -> Opt[Ip]
api.doc:
The client address from X-Forwarded-For by the rightmost-untrusted rule: the nearest address
that isn't one of the `trusted` proxies. Only meaningful behind a proxy that appends to the
header; sspur's server does not expose the peer address, so the nearest hop must be a proxy.

api.name: ip_from_hops
api.sig: fn ip_from_hops(req: Request, hops: Int where _ >= 1) -> Opt[Ip]
api.doc:
The client address `hops` entries from the right of X-Forwarded-For, for a fixed number of
proxies (express's `trust proxy = n`); the leftmost entry when there are fewer.

api.name: ip_from_header
api.sig: fn ip_from_header(req: Request, name: Str) -> Opt[Ip]
api.doc:
The address in a single-valued header such as X-Real-IP, CF-Connecting-IP or Fly-Client-IP.
Trust it only when the proxy in front always overwrites it.

api.name: Forwarded
api.sig: pub type Forwarded = {for_node: Opt[Str], by_node: Opt[Str], host: Opt[Str], proto: Opt[Str]} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
One element of a Forwarded header (RFC 7239): the `for`, `by`, `host` and `proto` parameters,
unquoted.

api.name: forwarded
api.sig: fn forwarded(req: Request) -> List[Forwarded]
api.doc: The elements of every Forwarded header of `req`, in order (nearest proxy last).

api.name: ip_from_forwarded
api.sig: fn ip_from_forwarded(req: Request, trusted: List[Cidr]) -> Opt[Ip]
api.doc:
The client address from Forwarded `for=` values by the rightmost-untrusted rule. `unknown`
and obfuscated identifiers (`_hidden`) are not addresses and stop the walk.

api.name: ip_key
api.sig: fn ip_key(ip: Ip) -> Str
api.doc: The key for one address: `ip:` and its canonical text (IPv4-mapped addresses as IPv4).

api.name: network_key
api.sig: fn network_key(ip: Ip, v4_bits: Int where _ >= 0 and _ <= 32, v6_bits: Int where _ >= 0 and _ <= 128) -> Str
api.doc:
The key for the network of an address, so that one client can't escape the limit by rotating
addresses within its allocation: the first `v4_bits` of IPv4, `v6_bits` of IPv6 (often 64).

api.name: route_key
api.sig: fn route_key(req: Request) -> Str
api.doc: The key of a route: the method and the path without the query.

api.name: compose_key
api.sig: fn compose_key(parts: List[Str]) -> Str
api.doc:
One key from several parts (a user, a route, an address), unambiguously: each part is prefixed
with its length, so `["a|b", "c"]` and `["a", "b|c"]` differ.

api.name: valid_policy_name
api.sig: fn valid_policy_name(s: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `s` can name a policy in the RateLimit headers: 1 to 64 printable ASCII characters.

api.name: policy_header
api.sig: fn policy_header(name: Str where valid_policy_name(_), p: Policy) -> (Str, Str)
api.doc:
The `RateLimit-Policy` field of draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers for one policy: its name,
`q` the quota and `w` the window in seconds.

api.name: policies_header
api.sig: fn policies_header(ps: List[(Str, Policy)]) -> (Str, Str)
api.doc: The `RateLimit-Policy` field listing several policies that apply to a request.

api.name: ratelimit_header
api.sig: fn ratelimit_header(name: Str where valid_policy_name(_), d: Decision) -> (Str, Str)
api.doc:
The `RateLimit` field for a decision under the policy `name`: `r` the remaining quota and `t`
the seconds until it resets.

api.name: with_partition
api.sig: fn with_partition(h: (Str, Str), key: Str) -> (Str, Str)
api.doc:
Adds the partition key parameter `pk` (an sf-binary of the key's bytes) to a RateLimit or
RateLimit-Policy field, for clients that share a quota with others.

api.name: legacy_headers
api.sig: fn legacy_headers(d: Decision, now_ms: Int) -> List[(Str, Str)]
api.doc:
The legacy fields many clients read (GitHub, express-rate-limit): X-RateLimit-Limit,
X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset, the last as Unix seconds of the reset.

api.name: retry_after_secs
api.sig: fn retry_after_secs(d: Decision) -> Int
api.doc:
The seconds a denied client should wait, rounded up and at least 1; 0 when allowed or when the
request can never succeed.

api.name: retry_after
api.sig: fn retry_after(d: Decision) -> Opt[(Str, Str)]
api.doc: The Retry-After field (RFC 9110 10.2.3, delay-seconds) of a denied decision.

api.name: HeaderStyle
api.sig: pub type HeaderStyle = DraftHeaders | LegacyHeaders | BothHeaders | NoHeaders derive Eq, Show
api.doc: Which rate limit fields a response carries.

api.name: headers
api.sig: fn headers(style: HeaderStyle, name: Str where valid_policy_name(_), p: Policy, d: Decision, now_ms: Int) -> List[(Str, Str)]
api.doc:
The fields for a decision in a style: the draft's RateLimit-Policy and RateLimit, the legacy
X-RateLimit fields, both, or none; Retry-After is added by `too_many`.

api.name: too_many
api.sig: fn too_many(style: HeaderStyle, name: Str where valid_policy_name(_), p: Policy, d: Decision, now_ms: Int, problem: Bool) -> Response
api.doc:
A 429 Too Many Requests response (RFC 6585) with Retry-After, the rate limit fields of
`style`, `cache-control: no-store`, and a text body, or with `problem` an RFC 9457
application/problem+json body.

api.name: Guard
api.sig: pub type Guard = {name: Str where valid_policy_name(_), policy: Policy, cost: Int where _ >= 1, style: HeaderStyle, skip_paths: List[Str], skip_methods: List[Str], allow_keys: List[Str], problem: Bool, fail_open: Bool} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
How a wrapper limits requests: the policy and its name in the headers, the cost of a request,
the header style, requests that are not limited (paths starting with one of `skip_paths`,
methods in `skip_methods`, keys in `allow_keys`), whether 429s are problem+json, and whether a
store failure lets the request through (`fail_open`) or answers 503.

api.name: guard
api.sig: fn guard(name: Str where valid_policy_name(_), p: Policy) -> Guard
api.doc:
A guard with the defaults: cost 1, draft headers, CORS preflights (OPTIONS) not limited, text
429s, and fail closed.

api.name: skipped
api.sig: fn skipped(g: Guard, req: Request, key: Str) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `g` leaves the request with key `key` alone.

api.name: enforce
api.sig: fn enforce[e](g: Guard, d: Decision, now_ms: Int, req: Request, next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Response ! e
api.doc:
Applies a decision: an allowed request goes to `next` and its response gets the rate limit
fields; a denied one gets `too_many`. This is the core the wrappers share, for limiters of
your own.

api.name: limit_memory
api.sig: fn limit_memory[e](t: Table, g: Guard, key: Request -> Str, next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e, conc, div, time
api.doc:
Wraps `next` with a limit kept in the in-memory table `t`, per key that `key` gives for a
request. Build it inside the handler (`req => ratelimit.limit_memory(t, g, ratelimit.route_key,
api)(req)`): handlers may not share function values.

api.name: limit_sql
api.sig: fn limit_sql[e](s: SqlStore, g: Guard, key: Request -> Str, next: Request -> Response ! e) -> Request -> Response ! e, db, time
api.doc:
Wraps `next` with a limit kept in the SQLite store `s`. A database error answers 503, or with
`fail_open` passes the request through unlimited.
